# Authentication Configuration
# ============================================
# Active provider
# Supported values: igrp-auth | none
AUTH_PROVIDER=igrp-auth

# IGRP Auth Client ID - The client identifier registered on your authorization server
# Example: igrp-example
IGRP_AUTH_CLIENT_ID=

# IGRP Auth Client Secret - The secret key for your IGRP Auth client
IGRP_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=

# IGRP Auth Issuer - Base URL of your authorization server (without trailing slash)
# The framework appends /.well-known/openid-configuration for OIDC discovery
# Example: http://auth.example.com  (discovery at http://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration)
IGRP_AUTH_ISSUER=

# IGRP Auth Scopes - Space-separated list of OAuth2 scopes to request.
# Must match scopes registered on the OAuth client AND advertised by the IdP.
# IGRP's discovery doc advertises `openid` only — requesting extra scopes
# (e.g. `profile`, `email`) is either silently dropped or rejected per Spring
# Authorization Server config. Register additional scopes on the client first.
# Defaults to "openid" if not set.
IGRP_AUTH_SCOPES=openid

# Two URIs must be registered on your authorization server (BOTH are required —
# missing either causes silent failures: login loops back to /login, or logout
# leaves the IdP SSO session active even though local cookies were cleared).
#
# With NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH unset:
#   - OAuth callback URI:    http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/igrp-auth
#   - Post-logout redirect:  http://localhost:3000/login
#
# With NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=/apps/template (the demo-legacy default):
#   - OAuth callback URI:    http://localhost:3000/apps/template/api/auth/callback/igrp-auth
#   - Post-logout redirect:  http://localhost:3000/apps/template/login
#
# Both must be configured on the client (e.g. `igrp-access-management` in IGRP
# Access Management). The OIDC spec requires byte-for-byte match.
#
# The IGRP provider enables PKCE (RFC 7636, S256) and OIDC `nonce` on the
# authorization-code exchange. No client-side configuration is required, but
# NEXTAUTH_URL, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, and the reverse-proxy path must remain
# stable across the /authorize → /callback round-trip — the PKCE/state/nonce
# cookies are JWE-encrypted with NEXTAUTH_SECRET and scoped to the
# NEXTAUTH_URL path. Mismatches surface as PKCE_ERROR / OAUTH_CALLBACK_ERROR
# at the callback step rather than as IdP-side rejections.

# ============================================
# NextAuth Configuration
# ============================================
# NextAuth URL - The public URL where your application is accessible
# Example: https://myapp.example.com or http://localhost:3000
NEXTAUTH_URL=

# NextAuth Secret - A random secret string used to encrypt JWT tokens and cookies
# Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 32
# Or use: https://generate-secret.vercel.app/32
NEXTAUTH_SECRET=

# NextAuth Internal URL - Internal URL for server-to-server communication
# Usually same as NEXTAUTH_URL, but can be different in Docker/K8s environments
# Example: http://localhost:3000 (for local) or http://nextjs-service:3000 (for K8s)
NEXTAUTH_URL_INTERNAL=

# Session refetch interval (seconds) for the client session poll. Each poll
# hits /api/auth/session and triggers a silent access-token refresh when the
# token is near/after expiry. MUST be strictly less than 60 (the framework's
# proactive-refresh buffer). If set >= 60, client polls will not fire proactively
# before the token's expiry window and refreshes will race against an already-
# expired cookie. Recommended: 45. Unset / non-numeric / <= 0 falls back to 45.
IGRP_SESSION_REFETCH_INTERVAL=45

# Optional NextAuth session-cookie lifetime (seconds). Align to your IdP's
# refresh-token lifetime so the session cookie expires with the refresh token
# instead of NextAuth's ~30-day default. Leave unset to keep the default.
# IGRP_SESSION_MAX_AGE=28800

# ============================================
# IGRP Framework Configuration
# ============================================
# IGRP Access Manager API - Base URL for the IGRP App Manager API
# Example: https://api.example.com/igrp-manager
IGRP_ACCESS_MANAGEMENT_API=

# IGRP App Code - Unique identifier for your application in the IGRP framework
# Example: demo-app | DEMO_APP | APP-DEMO
IGRP_APP_CODE=

# IGRP Preview Mode - Enable preview mode to skip authentication checks
# Set to true to disable authentication (useful for development/demo)
# Set to false or leave empty to enable authentication
# Values: true or false (case-insensitive, handles quotes)
IGRP_PREVIEW_MODE=

# Enable Access Management synchronization
# When set to true, the framework syncs the application, resources/routes,
# and on-code menus with the IGRP Access Management API at startup. Sync is
# scheduled post-response via `after()` so it never blocks the first request.
# Values: true or false
IGRP_SYNC_ACCESS=

# Enable on-code menus synchronization
# When set to true, the framework pushes `src/temp/menus/menus.ts`
# (IGRP_DEFAULT_MENU) to Access Management at startup via
# syncApplicationMenus. Requires IGRP_SYNC_ACCESS=true and
# IGRP_PREVIEW_MODE=false to take effect.
# When false (default), AM remains the source of truth and no push happens.
# NOTE: enabling this overwrites the menus on the AM side with the local array.
# Values: true or false

# Sync menu<->role assignments during the on-code menu push
# Forwarded as the `syncRoles` argument of syncApplicationMenus. When true,
# Access Management also reconciles the menu role assignments; when false,
# only the menu entries are synced and existing role assignments are kept.
# Only consulted when IGRP_SYNC_ON_CODE_MENUS=true and the push actually runs.
# When unset, defaults to true (the AM client default) — set to false to opt out.
# Values: true or false

# Internationalization (i18n) The Application Center uses **next-intl 4 without i18n routing**: the locale is resolved per request and never appears in the URL. The platform default is *not* part of the fallback chain (FR-13). `en.json` and `fr.json` are **partial by design** (FR-5) — today they only carry the language-selector strings. #   With NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH unset:           http://localhost:3000/api/auth

# Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 32

NEXTAUTH_SECRET=

# Usually same as NEXTAUTH_URL, but can be different in Docker/K8s environments

# lifetime — IGRP Access Management ends every session after 8 h
# (absolute-timeout-seconds=28800) — so the cookie, and the session-store entry
# below, expire with the session instead of lingering for NextAuth's ~30-day
# default after the IdP has already ended it. Recommended: 28800.
# IGRP_SESSION_MAX_AGE=28800

# Server-side session store (Redis). REQUIRED when the app runs MORE THAN ONE
# REPLICA or shares its domain with other IGRP apps; optional for a single
# replica on its own domain. In production, the app logs a warning once when
# it writes a session without a store. When set, the session's tokens
# are kept in Redis and the session cookie carries only a session id — a few
# hundred bytes instead of 3–4 KB. Set it whenever several apps share one
# domain (an app center at `/` plus apps under `/apps/*`): their cookies share
# the browser's cookie jar, and without a store they push the Cookie header
# past the 8 KB limit of nginx and other proxies
# (`400 Request Header Or Cookie Too Large`). With several replicas and no
# store, two replicas can refresh the same session at once with the same
# refresh token; the IdP treats that as token reuse and revokes the session.
# Every replica of the app must point at the same Redis. Values are encrypted
# with NEXTAUTH_SECRET before they reach Redis. If Redis is down, sessions are
# written to the cookie again (bigger) and existing store-backed sessions sign
# in again. Leave unset to keep the tokens in the cookie.
# Reusing an existing Redis is fine: pick a separate logical database (the
# number at the end of the URL) and, ideally, a dedicated ACL user limited to
# the store's keys and commands:
#   ACL SETUSER igrp-frontend on >password ~igrp:session:* +get +set +del +eval +select +ping +client|setinfo
# Example: redis://igrp-frontend:password@redis.demo-igrp-stack.svc:6379/1

# Silent token refresh is scheduled adaptively by IGRPSessionWatcher from
# `session.expiresAt`, so it retunes itself on every rotation. The fixed
# SessionProvider poll is only a last-resort backstop and is set in
# `src/lib/config/get-session-args.ts`. An earlier IGRP_SESSION_REFETCH_INTERVAL

# Internationalisation (i18n)

The app uses **next-intl 4 without i18n routing** through `@igrp/framework-next/i18n`: the locale is resolved per request and never appears in the URL. The framework owns the mechanics (cookie, providers, format helpers, CLI); its guide is `templates/demo-v1/docs/I18N.md` in [igrp-framework-nextjs](https://git.nosi.cv/igrp-3_0/igrp-framework-frontend/igrp-framework-nextjs). This page covers what is specific to the Application Center.

## Model

| Concept | Value |
|---|---|
| Platform locales | `pt`, `en`, `fr`. Fixed. |
| Default locale | `pt`. Its catalog (`messages/pt.json`) is complete and types every key. |
| Format locales | `pt-CV`, `en-GB`, `fr-FR` by default; per deployment via `IGRP_FORMAT_LOCALES` (always region-qualified, e.g. `pt-PT`). Drive dates, numbers and `<html lang>`. |
| Time zone | `IGRP_TIME_ZONE`, default `Atlantic/Cape_Verde`. Applies on server and browser. |
| Resolution | **Session-first**: `session.user.locale` → `IGRP_LOCALE` cookie → `Accept-Language` → `pt`. |

`IGRP_FORMAT_LOCALES` and `IGRP_TIME_ZONE` are the only formatting settings and are read only in `src/i18n/index.ts` (see `.env.example`).

## Where each piece lives

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/i18n/index.ts` | `igrpDefineI18n(...)`: locales, format locales, time zone, `getSessionLocale`, `persistLocale`. Server-only; middleware must not import it. |
| `src/i18n/request.ts` | next-intl request config, registered in `next.config.ts`. |
| `src/i18n/actions.ts` | `setLocale` server action, passed to the switchers. |
| `src/i18n/global.d.ts` | Types `useTranslations` keys from `pt.json` plus the framework namespaces. |
| `src/i18n/status.ts` | `useStatusLabel`, `useStatusOptions`: translated labels for API status codes (`common.status.*`). |
| `src/i18n/session-locale-switcher.tsx` | Switcher for authenticated pages; awaits the session update before the refresh. |
| `src/i18n/messages/{pt,en,fr}.json` | Catalogs. One top-level namespace per feature, nested camelCase keys, ICU. |

## Changing the language

- **Saving.** `persistLocale` calls `PUT /api/users/me/locale` (`updateCurrentUserLocale` in `src/actions/access-client.ts`). It skips the API when there is no session or auth bypass is on; then only the cookie changes.
- **Cookie sync.** `src/middleware.ts` calls `igrpSyncLocaleCookie` with the token's locale (`resolution: "session-first"`), so sessionless pages such as login follow the user's choice.
- **Switchers.** The authenticated layout (`src/app/(igrp)/layout.tsx`) and the invite layout (invite visitors have a session) use `SessionLocaleSwitcher`; only login uses the plain `IGRPLocaleSwitcher`.

## Translating a feature

1. Add a camelCase namespace (`oauthClients`, `serviceAccounts`) to `pt.json`, `en.json` and `fr.json`. `check-catalogs` fails on any key missing from en or fr.
2. Translate every user-facing string: JSX text, `aria-label`, `title`, `placeholder`, toasts, confirm dialogs, empty states, column headers, Zod messages.
3. Keep the pt wording exactly as the literal it replaces. Do not swap in a shared key whose text differs (`common.unknownError` is not "Erro desconhecido"); add a feature key.
4. Client: `useTranslations("ns")`. Server: `await getTranslations("ns")` from `next-intl/server`.
5. Zod schemas take a translator (`(key) => string`) instead of literals (see `src/features/applications/app-schemas.ts`). API enum codes map to keys in a per-feature `lib/i18n.ts` (see `src/features/users/lib/i18n.ts`). Status codes stay API values; use `useStatusLabel` / `useStatusOptions`.
6. Dates, numbers, sorting: `useIGRPFormat()` (client) or `igrpFormatDate(value, await igrpResolveFormatLocale(i18n), undefined, i18n.timeZone)` (server). Never `useFormatter` and never a hardcoded region.
7. Add the feature's folders to the `lint:i18n` script in `package.json`.
8. Delete dead files instead of translating them (grep `src` for importers first).

## Checks

`pnpm lint:i18n` (also part of `build`) runs `igrp-i18n check-catalogs` (orphan keys, invalid ICU, argument parity with `pt`, coverage) and `igrp-i18n check-literals` over the folders listed in `package.json`, which include `src/components`. Mark a literal that is not language (a parsed token, a fixed formatter locale) with `// igrp-i18n-ignore: <why>`.

`src/__tests__/i18n/catalogs.test.ts` fails when an en value equals its pt value, to catch English text left in pt. Genuine cognates and protocol terms go in its `ALLOWED` list.

## Testing

`src/test-setup.ts` wraps every render in `IGRPIntlTestProvider` with `pt`, so existing assertions use pt text. To render another locale:

```tsx
import { renderWithIntl } from "@/__tests__/helpers/intl";
renderWithIntl(<Page />, { locale: "en" });
```

Add one English-render test per feature's main page, plus one for any dialog or form with its own strings. Build mock data at module scope: unstable mocked query data makes Vitest run out of memory.

## Release notes

- `NEXT_PUBLIC_AUDIT_TIME_ZONE` was removed. `IGRP_TIME_ZONE` now drives all date and time formatting. The default is `Atlantic/Cape_Verde`; an invalid value logs a warning and falls back to the default.
- The language is session-first: the choice is saved to the user profile and read back from the session.
- The app now runs on `@igrp/framework-next` 0.2.0-beta.12 and design system beta.8.
